minutes.headline: Select Board set Special Town Meeting for Jan 7 and the special election for Jan 11 on the school project.
minutes.summary: The board approved a Salvation Army boot drive, heard a police K9 grant proposal with a demonstration, and took committee reports including a school building project update. It reviewed the town manager's and its own goals, set the special town meeting and election dates, and cut the Green Communities task force from seven to five members.

Reduce the Green Communities task force membership from seven to five

budget_items.what_was_said: Grant would cover most start-up costs of a police canine program over three years, with a five-year town commitment sought.
Estimated annual food, veterinary and in-service training costs after the grant, with business partners hoped to offset them.
Each month of delay is projected to add cost to the school building project.
The revised design would cut cost by over a million dollars and lower the per-household impact.
The scope and budget agreement was said to total a figure in the mid-thirties of millions.
The town received participation credits last year, and an in-house grant program using them was suggested.
The town's current animal control cost was compared with nearby towns for a regional approach.
Water department warrant for quarterly bills.
Accounts payable and payroll warrants were read, including a negative payroll for a disability retirement.
A 30-year term would cost the average homeowner more over time than 20 years.

decisions.decision: Board had no objection to the citizens' group putting up Christmas lights at the center of town; no vote needed.
The K9 grant item was informational only; the board expressed support but no vote was required.
Warrant to open November 12 and close November 19; draft election question to come next week.
Town manager to find the senior abatement information and email it to the board.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to set a special town meeting for Tuesday, January 7 and a special election for Saturday, January 11.
The board voted to reduce the Green Communities task force from seven members to five.
The warrant is to open November 12 and close November 19, and a draft election question is due next week.
The board heard a police K9 grant proposal with a demonstration; it was informational and no vote was taken.
A motion on the Salvation Army boot drive was made, but the result is not audible in the recording.

why_it_matters: The January dates set when residents will be asked to vote on the school building project, which affects local tax bills through the town's borrowing.

The minutes record that delay is projected to add cost to the school project and that a 30-year borrowing term would cost the average homeowner more over time than 20 years, so the election question and term bear on what households pay.
The K9 proposal sought a five-year town commitment for ongoing costs once the grant ends, which would fall on the town budget, mostly taxes, if adopted.
watch_next: The draft election question, due at the board's next meeting.
The warrant for the special town meeting, which closes November 19.
